title: Lord, a Band of Foes Increasing
description: Lord, a Band of Foes Increasing in Tonic Solfa to GALILEE (JUDE), doh is Ab: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 5 verses and a piano.
about: John Brownlie translated these words from the Greek service books for Hymns from the Morningland (Paisley, 1911), headed “Psalm II”.
The book printed the words without tunes. They are in Eights and Sevens (8.7.8.7), and this page sets them to GALILEE (JUDE); any other Eights and Sevens tune fits them as well.
underlay: Lord, a band of foes in-creas-ing Ter-ror to my heart would bring; For they tell my soul un-ceas-ing, That no help from God can spring.

lines: Lord, a band of foes increasing
Terror to my heart would bring;
For they tell my soul unceasing,
That no help from God can spring.
Yet Thou art my shield about me,
Till the time of strife is past;
And though cruel foes may flout me,
Thou wilt hear my prayer at last.
On my couch when night was falling,
Lay I down devoid of fear;
And when morning light was calling,
I awoke, for thou wert near.
Tens of thousands round my dwelling
Stand arrayed to do me harm;
But my trust when foes are swelling,
Rests in Thine almighty arm.
Rise, O Lord, for Thou, victorious,
Hast the might of sin o'erthrown,
And amid Thy triumph glorious,
Bless the people Thou dost own.

source: John Brownlie, Hymns from the Morningland (1911)
licence: Public domain: John Brownlie died in 1925.
credits: Translated by John Brownlie (1857–1925) from the Greek, public domain, as printed in Hymns from the Morningland; set to GALILEE (JUDE) by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
